title: Outlook: admin policy for "Days of email to save" in new Outlook for Windows offline settings
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap facts and existing offline-control command are supported, and searches found no published configuration for the planned days-of-email policy. Minor corrections should add supporting references and the omitted Access heading in the admin path. The November 20 release notes do not announce this policy.

claims.claim: Days of email to save determines how many days of email are saved locally for offline access.
claims.quote:
Select the number of days to save emails locally:
1. Select Settings > General > Offline > Days of email to save.
2. From the dropdown, select 7, 30 (this is the default value), 90, or 180 days of email to save.
claims.fix: Add https://support.microsoft.com/office/2460e4a8-16c7-47fc-b204-b1549275aac9, titled 'How to work offline in Outlook for Windows', to sources for the existing local-save behaviour.

claims.claim: Microsoft's classic Outlook Cached Exchange Mode guidance warns that raising the sync window through Group Policy triggers full OST resynchronisation.
claims.quote: When GPO changes SyncWindowSetting to any higher value, Outlook will do a full OST resynchronization when the new value applies.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated that the planned new Outlook policy causes the classic Outlook full-resynchronisation behaviour.
claims.quote: Searched: new Outlook offline policy existing users values. Read only-subset-items-synchronized, policy-management, Set-OwaMailboxPolicy and new Outlook release notes; full OST resynchronisation is described for classic Outlook Group Policy, not this planned policy.

claims.claim: Most new Outlook mailbox policies apply to both Outlook on the web and new Outlook for Windows rather than being independently enabled per client.
claims.quote: Most of the mailbox policies apply to both Outlook on the web and new Outlook for Windows, so you can't enable them on one client but not the other.
claims.fix: Keep the cited 'most' wording, but add: 'The Exchange overview instead states that all mailbox policies set for Outlook on the web also affect new Outlook for Windows.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/exchange/clients-and-mobile-in-exchange-online/outlook-on-the-web/outlook-web-app-mailbox-policies.

claims.quote: In the EAC, go to Roles > Outlook web app policies. ... Access: Select Manage access. In the Edit access flyout that opens, the available settings are visible in the following sections: ... Offline access

claims.claim: Set-OwaMailboxPolicy -OfflineEnabledWin $false is an Exchange PowerShell operation that blocks new Outlook's offline use.
claims.quote: The OfflineEnabledWin parameter specifies whether offline capabilities are available in Outlook (formerly known as the new Outlook for Windows) ... $false: Users can't manage offline capabilities in Outlook. No items are saved to the user's device.

claims.claim: OfflineEnabledWin allows or blocks offline capabilities rather than setting the number of days to save.
claims.quote: The OfflineEnabledWin parameter on the Set-OwaMailboxPolicy cmdlet allows or blocks the new Outlook for Windows from being used offline.

claims.claim: The existing mailbox-policy control can govern a group of users.
